decision: Black Friday pages are pre-rendered with the new price book and switched on at 00:00 by configuration, not by a mass cache purge
why: Purging millions of pages at midnight would send the whole audience to the origin at the worst moment.
value: The midnight spike lands on the cache, and no order is taken at a wrong price.

decision: Admission control at a load-tested limit: new checkouts wait in a signed first-come line while bags stay reserved
why: Past saturation, response time grows without bound and every checkout slows down.
alternative: Let everyone in and rely on autoscaling.
value: Checkout stays inside its tested envelope; waiting never costs the item.

decision: Hot deals use sharded in-memory counters with a reservation timeout, and a database ledger as the truth
why: One inventory row serializes every buyer of a doorbuster; overselling means refunds and complaints.
alternative: Row locks, optimistic retries, or oversell and cancel.
value: Zero oversold units, at the cost of a brief undersell of the last few.

decision: Two payment providers with health-based routing, and a capped rules fallback if fraud scoring slows
why: A payment brownout is the most expensive failure of the night.
alternative: One provider and a status page.
value: Approval rate is protected when either provider degrades.

decision: A five-level degradation plan, decided in October, automatic at level 1 and human-approved beyond
why: Decisions under stress are worse, and flags have to be tested in both states before the night.
value: The site gets simpler under pressure instead of breaking, and the buy button never switches off.

decision: Readiness is sized by expected lost sales, not by peak capacity for its own sake
why: Spending is justified only while each real of readiness removes more than a real of expected loss.
alternative: Provision for the worst case all year.
value: Cost becomes a design input the business can reason about.
